subject: binary data - fitting curves, jittering and facet wrapping

messages.author: 7a2c097f8b936c87
messages.subject: binary data - fitting curves, jittering and facet wrapping
parts:
Hello,

I'm a ggplot newbie, so please bear with me.  I've searched around, and while the info is surely out there, I haven't come across it.

I have tree mortality data (binary) and would like to plot precipitation vs. mortality, facet-wrapped for each species, along with a smoother with confidence intervals.  What I've come up with so far is:

    ggplot(trees$mort, aes(x = precip, y = mort)) + geom_point() + geom_rug(position='jitter') + facet_wrap(~species)

I have a few questions I was hoping the list might help with:
    1) My x and y scales are quite different, so the rug jitter is drastically different in the two axes.  Is there any way other than scaling the variables themselves to normalize the jitter across axes?
    2) I'd like to put the wrapped species in a particular order - can this be controlled?
    3) I'd like to add a smooth curve fit with confidence intervals to the binary points.  Is there a way to put a smoothed line on this kind of data, or will I have to fit a model first?

thanks,
allie

> On 7 sep, 05:14, Alexander Shenkin <ashen...@ufl.edu> wrote:
>> Hello,
>>
>> I'm a ggplot newbie, so please bear with me. I've searched around, and
>> while the info is surely out there, I haven't come across it.
>>
>> I have tree mortality data (binary) and would like to plot precipitation
>> vs. mortality, facet-wrapped for each species, along with a smoother
>> with confidence intervals. What I've come up with so far is:
>>
>> ggplot(trees$mort, aes(x = precip, y = mort)) + geom_point() +
>> geom_rug(position='jitter') + facet_wrap(~species)
>>
>> I have a few questions I was hoping the list might help with:
>> 1) My x and y scales are quite different, so the rug jitter is
>> drastically different in the two axes. Is there any way other than
>> scaling the variables themselves to normalize the jitter across axes?

>> 2) I'd like to put the wrapped species in a particular order - can
>> this be controlled?

reorder the factor levels of the species, e.g.

mydata <- transform(mydata, species=reorder(species,popdensity))

>> 3) I'd like to add a smooth curve fit with confidence intervals to
>> the binary points. Is there a way to put a smoothed line on this kind
>> of data, or will I have to fit a model first?

Probably the best way to add a smooth for binary data is
geom_smooth(method="gam",family="binomial") [you may need to explicitly
load the mgcv package first].

>> thanks,
